staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this preserved vulnerable checkout. Its `pack.c` line map matches the staged vulnerable `mrb_read_int()` path and the saved AddressSanitizer stack reaches `str_init_embed()` in this source tree.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer `SEGV` caused by a WRITE in `str_init_embed()`. Source analysis shows that `read_tmpl()` accepts an oversized decimal template count above `INT_MAX`, narrows it into `int count` without a range check, and then `mrb_str_new()` reaches `str_init_embed()` with that invalid length, where the terminator write goes out of bounds.

bug_description.original: An index-out-of-bounds write in mruby's pack/unpack handling: malformed pack templates can cause unpack_hex / pack_unpack (mrbgems/mruby-pack/src/pack.c) to drive string creation with an incorrect size, leading to an out-of-bounds write in str_new -> str_init_embed (src/mruby/src/string.c). This can crash the process (SIGSEGV) and cause memory corruption, potentially enabling further exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is plain mruby source, so `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()` routes it down the Ruby-source parser path and VM execution reaches `String#unpack`. On the witnessed path the script calls `unpacktest []," ","h3333339010"`, so `prepare_tmpl()` binds the attacker-controlled template string and `read_tmpl()` parses directive `h` plus the exact decimal suffix `3333339010`. Vulnerable `read_tmpl()` only checks whether `mrb_read_int()` failed; it does not reject successfully parsed `mrb_int n` values above `INT_MAX`, even though the staged patch adds exactly that missing `INT_MAX < n` guard. The next line narrows that oversized positive `mrb_int` into `int count`, stores it through `*countp`, and `pack_unpack()` forwards the caller-side `count` to `unpack_hex()`. `unpack_hex()` then uses that invalid count as the requested length in `mrb_str_new(mrb, NULL, count)`. The saved AddressSanitizer stack proves this path reaches `str_new()` and then `str_init_embed()`, where `RSTR_EMBED_PTR(s)[len] = '\0';` performs the crashing WRITE.

source.description: First project-code consumption of the attacker-controlled unpack template. `String#unpack` binds the Ruby template argument into `tmpl->str`, which `read_tmpl()` then parses into the directive and oversized decimal count that drive the crash.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `9464f73c024ae893753a9b52beef75220b98a9db785573cc703141a3f6207974`. Its load-bearing call site is `unpacktest []," ","h3333339010"`, so this statement receives the exact attacker-controlled template string `h3333339010`.

sink.description: Crash sink. The invalid length propagated from the oversized template count reaches embedded-string initialization, and this terminator write performs the saved invalid WRITE.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. `read_tmpl()` rejects only parse failure, not the case where parsed `mrb_int n` is larger than `INT_MAX`, so the following `count = (int)n;` narrows an out-of-range attacker-controlled size into `int`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Ruby execution reaches `String#unpack` and hands the attacker-controlled template object to the pack parser here. The later parsed `mrb_int n`, narrowed `count`, and invalid string length all originate from this bound template string.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific format gate. The witness begins with Ruby source text rather than a `RITE` bytecode header, so this predicate selects the source parser path that can execute the script's `String#unpack` call.

admitted_location.code: return mrb_load_exec(mrb, mrb_parse_file_continue(mrb, fp, leading.b, bufsize, c), c);

coarse_trace.summary: The staged file is admitted as plain Ruby source rather than a `.mrb` bytecode image, and execution reaches the script's `String#unpack` call.
The template parser reads directive `h`, parses the exact suffix `3333339010`, misses the `INT_MAX` bound, and narrows that oversized `mrb_int` into `int count`.
The narrowed `count` is written through `*countp`, received by the caller's local `count`, and forwarded into `unpack_hex()` as the requested string length.
The invalid length reaches `mrb_str_new()`, the saved crash path continues into `str_init_embed()`, and the embedded-string terminator write matches the AddressSanitizer invalid WRITE.

fine_trace.note: Source. `String#unpack` binds the exact attacker-controlled template argument into `tmpl->str`. For the witnessed script this value is the literal `h3333339010`.
The parser reads the first template character from `tmpl->str`; on this witness `t == 'h'`, which selects the hex-unpack directive.
Because `t == 'h'`, the parser selects `PACK_DIR_HEX` and marks the suffix as a count-bearing width for the later `unpack_hex()` call.
The suffix parser consumes the decimal tail `3333339010` and materializes it as `mrb_int n == 3333339010`; `e` advances past the last digit.
Root cause. Because `mrb_read_int()` succeeds, this guard falls through even though `n` exceeds `INT_MAX`. The staged patch adds the missing range check at this exact decision point.
The accepted oversized positive `mrb_int` is narrowed into local `int count` with no range guard. Because `n > INT_MAX`, this conversion no longer preserves the requested positive width.
The narrowed local `count` is exported through the output parameter, making the caller's `count` variable carry the invalid width derived from the oversized suffix.
The caller receives the callee-produced width through `&count`; from this point, `pack_unpack()`'s local `count` is the same invalid value written via `*countp`.

fine_trace.code: srcidx += unpack_hex(mrb, sptr, srclen - srcidx, result, count, flags);
fine_trace.note: With `dir == PACK_DIR_HEX`, `pack_unpack()` forwards the caller-side `count` into `unpack_hex()` as the requested output width.

The invalid `count` is reused directly as the requested length for a new Ruby string. Here `p` is `NULL`, so later embedded-string initialization will not copy bytes but will still trust the length for terminator placement.

The saved crash stack proves this `mrb_str_new()` call continues into `str_init_embed()`. Source shows that any negative `len` satisfies `RSTR_EMBEDDABLE_P(len)` because the macro is only `((len) <= RSTRING_EMBED_LEN_MAX)`.

Sink. Because `p == NULL`, the guarded `memcpy` is skipped and this terminator write is the first memory access in `str_init_embed()`. On the observed crash path, the invalid length writes outside the embedded buffer and matches the saved AddressSanitizer WRITE.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the root cause because it adds `|| INT_MAX < n` to the failing guard in `read_tmpl()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

format.name: Plain mruby source file
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42517942/poc`. Its load-bearing property on the vulnerable path is the literal `String#unpack` template `h3333339010` applied to the one-byte string `" "`: directive `h` selects `unpack_hex`, and the exact decimal suffix `3333339010` is large enough to parse successfully as `mrb_int` while still exceeding the `INT_MAX` bound that the patch later adds before `count = (int)n;`.
